coverage_notes:
SOURCING. The backbone of this dataset is Georgia's own football staff directory captured by the Wayback Machine twice during the title season: 2021-10-27 (in-season, 56 people) and 2021-12-28 (13 days before the CFP National Championship, 54 people). Both pages are explicitly headed "2021 Football Coaching Staff" and "2021 Football Support Staff". Every one of the 56 rows below comes from those captures; nothing is inferred or padded.

WARNING ABOUT THE LIVE SCHOOL URL. The live page https://georgiadogs.com/sports/football/coaches/2021 is NOT a valid source for the 2021 season. It appears frozen mid-transition around Feb-Mar 2022: it lists 2022 hires (Bryan McClendon, Fran Brown, Stacy Searels, Chidera Uzo-Diribe, Mike Bobo, Will Muschamp as "Co-Defensive Coordinator") while omitting Dan Lanning, Cortez Hankton and Jahmile Addae, who actually coached the 2021 team. By contrast the site's /2016, /2020 and /2022 pages are period-correct. Anyone re-verifying this data should use the Wayback captures cited here, not the live /2021 URL.

QUOTE MECHANICS. The archived directory is a Sidearm Sports HTML table that renders each person's name and title in SEPARATE table cells, so no contiguous "Name — Title" string exists on the page. Each archived-page quote is therefore the exact, unmodified title text from that person's row, and the accompanying note names the row it belongs to. Where a person also appears in the Wikipedia article's roster-footer template, a second source quotes the raw wikitext line, which DOES contain name and role contiguously. Every quote in this dataset was programmatically verified to occur verbatim in the page it is attributed to.

DUPLICATE TITLES. Several titles repeat across rows ("Quality Control - Defense" x3, "Football Operations Assistant" x2, "Assistant Recruiting Coordinator" x2, "Assistant Strength & Conditioning Coach" x2). Those quotes match the page but do not uniquely identify the person on their own; the note field disambiguates, and the Wikipedia wikitext source resolves several of them by name.

NAME DISCREPANCIES. Wikipedia's roster footer spells the assistant S&C coach "Rodney Price"; Georgia's own directory and his staff-bio URL (/sports/football/roster/staff/rodney-prince/98) spell it "Rodney Prince" — I used the school's spelling. Wikipedia also lists Matt Godwin twice, under two different titles ("Player personnel coordinator" and "Director, player personnel"); Georgia's directory lists him once, as "Player Personnel Coordinator". Two staffers were renamed on the school site later (Hailey Hughes now appears as "Hailey Hunter", Angela Kirkpatrick as "Angela Ellington"); the 2021-era names are used here.

RING-RULE / MID-SEASON MOVEMENT. Josh Lee (Director of Football Operations) resigned in December 2021, per a DawgNation report dated December 21, 2021, and is absent from the 2021-12-28 capture — he was NOT on staff at the January 10, 2022 championship game and is flagged accordingly. Bryant Gross-Armiento is the one genuinely ambiguous case: present in the October capture, gone by the December capture; I could not find a dated report of his departure, and I ruled out the search-result claim that he was at Texas A&M in 2021 by checking A&M's own archived staff directories (Oct 2021, Jan 2022, Feb 2022, Apr 2022 — he appears in none). His championship-game status is unconfirmed. Dan Lanning was named Oregon's head coach on December 11, 2021 but remained Georgia's DC through the CFP and coached the title game; he is still listed in the December 28 capture.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT. (1) Graduate assistants — Georgia's public directory lists no GA rows at all, so the gradasst category is empty; this is a real gap, not an absence of GAs on the team. (2) Medical and athletic-training staff — Georgia's football staff page carries no trainers or physicians. Sports medicine (Ron Courson's group) sits in the athletics-wide staff directory rather than the football directory, so I did not have football-specific evidence and did not include them. The two nutrition roles are categorized as medical since that is the closest available bucket. (3) The 2021 media guide exists on Issuu (issuu.com/georgiadogs/docs/21fb_uga_football_guide) but its staff pages are not reliably text-extractable for verbatim quoting, so I did not cite it. (4) Titles are as of the in-season captures; a few people may have changed titles between October and the January title game, though the two captures show zero title changes for anyone appearing in both.
